reading.body:
The American Federation of Government Employees filed 18 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports naming AI, making it one of the more active union filers on the issue.

The filings are concentrated. Twenty-two of the 30 named lobbyists appear on 10 or more AI filings, and the top group of eight appears on 16 each. That is a single coordinated account rather than scattered individual registrations, which is what a large institutional client with an in-house government affairs operation looks like in LDA data.

For AI specifically, this matters because the federal workforce is both a regulator and a customer of AI. A union representing government employees has a direct interest in how agencies procure, deploy, and oversee automated systems, and in the rules that govern the people who run them. The filings show sustained attention, not a one-off comment.

What the data does not say is what AFGE argued. LDA reports record that a client lobbied on an issue, not the position taken, so the direction of the advocacy is invisible here. The data also covers only federal lobbying disclosures and only filings this site has tied to AI. It says nothing about compute, data centers, or power, and nothing about whether the lobbying succeeded.

summary: AMERICAN FED OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AFL-CIO filed 18 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 54302.
